steps.name: Sample structure QC
caveats: TPM is already within-sample scaled for length and depth; structure on this plot reflects expression differences. All 12 samples come from one batch, so strong non-condition clustering would indicate a sample identity issue rather than batch — flag it, do not silently drop samples.
steps.context: Inputs: /eval-four-models-v2-with-tpm-input-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/abundance/tpm.csv (12000 gene symbols x 12 samples of gene-level Salmon TPM; first column gene symbol, not yet on a log scale) and /eval-four-models-v2-with-tpm-input-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (one row per sample with a condition column: 6 lesional, 6 control). Design: unpaired, single batch, no known confounders; read the exact condition level names from metadata.csv. Transform TPM to log2(value+1) — the values are not log-scaled, so transform once; do NOT apply a count-model variance-stabilizing transformation (no raw counts exist). On the log matrix produce: MDS or PCA on the top 500 most variable genes, a sample-distance heatmap, and detected-gene counts per sample (TPM > 0), all colored by condition. Do not apply any between-sample normalization to the TPM.
steps.question: Do the 6 psoriasis lesional skin samples and 6 control samples separate by condition on log2(TPM+1) expression, and is any sample misclustered relative to its group?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC on log abundance values: MDS or PCA, sample distances, detected genes per R-0071@e4e2

steps.description: MDS/PCA and sample-distance QC on log2(TPM+1) expression, colored by psoriasis lesional vs control condition, to confirm the 6 vs 6 design and flag outliers before differential expression.
acceptance_criteria: MDS or PCA plot on log2(TPM+1) values of the top 500 most variable genes is produced, colored by condition (lesional vs control).
Sample distances and per-sample detected-gene counts are computed and reported.
An explicit statement is given: the 6 lesional and 6 control samples separate by condition, or the misclustered sample(s) are named.
The log2(TPM+1) matrix (12000 genes x 12 samples) is saved as the input for the DE step.

steps.name: limma linear model on log-scale expression values
caveats: Only a Salmon TPM table was delivered — no raw counts and no quantification directories. Per rule R-0004, count models (DESeq2, edgeR, voom, pydeseq2) are forbidden for this table; if raw counts or quantifications ever become available, a count-based fit is the preferred reroute.
log2FC on log2(TPM+1) is relative to the +1 offset; interpret it as an approximate effect size, not an exact log2 ratio of TPMs.
TPM is comparable only within a protocol; the data profile states a single Salmon protocol and a single batch, so no protocol or batch term is needed — state that assumption in the output.
steps.context: Use the log2(TPM+1) matrix and metadata from T1S1. (1) Low-abundance filter: keep genes with TPM >= 1 in at least 6 samples (the smallest group size); remove the rest; report the number of genes kept — limma has no independent filter, so this must precede the fit. (2) No between-sample normalization: TPM already carries within-sample length/depth scaling; do NOT apply TMM, DESeq2 size factors, or any other count-based normalization. (3) Design: condition factor with an explicit reference level control (do not rely on alphabetical level order); name the contrast lesional/control (factor_numerator_denominator) so a positive log2FC means higher expression in lesional. (4) Fit lmFit; run eBayes with trend=TRUE and robust=TRUE. (5) Results: topTable with adjust.method='BH'; select genes with adjusted p-value < 0.05. No LFC threshold was stated in the question, so do not run TREAT — record that the policy is test_against_threshold. (6) Output table columns: gene symbol, log2FC (lesional vs control), AveExpr, t, P.Value, adj.PValue. Do not use DESeq2, edgeR, or voom: TPM input violates the negative-binomial count model assumptions.
steps.question: Which genes differ in abundance between psoriasis lesional skin and control skin, by Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value from the limma fit on log2(TPM+1)?

grounding.reason: limma linear model on log-scale expression values per R-0072@881a

steps.description: TPM-filtered limma trend fit (contrast lesional vs control) producing the BH-adjusted differential expression table and the DE gene set.
acceptance_criteria: A per-gene results table (log2FC lesional vs control, AveExpr, t, P.Value, BH adj.PValue) is produced for all genes passing the TPM filter, and the number of genes tested is reported.
The DE gene set is defined as BH adj.PValue < 0.05 and saved, with counts of genes up- and down-regulated in lesional skin.
The design formula, reference level (control), contrast name, and limma options (trend=TRUE, robust=TRUE) are recorded in the step output.

steps.name: Report
steps.context: Assemble the final report from the T1S1 and T1S2 outputs: method (limma linear model on log2(TPM+1) with trend=TRUE, robust=TRUE), package versions, design formula and contrast (reference: control, contrast lesional/control), thresholds (BH adj.PValue < 0.05; no LFC threshold because none was stated), the number of genes tested after the TPM filter (>=1 TPM in >=6 of 12 samples) and the number of DE genes up/down in lesional skin, top DE genes per direction (top 20 by adj.PValue), the MDS/PCA from QC with the condition-separation statement, and the explicit caveat that only a Salmon TPM table was delivered (no raw counts or quantification directories), which is why count models were excluded. Reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, the random seed for any randomized QC step (e.g., most-variable-gene selection), and the reference organism (Homo sapiens; gene symbols as delivered). Store the record with the results.
steps.question: What is the final answer to 'which genes differ between the lesional and the control samples', and what is its reproducibility record?
constraints: report: report_fields = method, versions, design, thresholds, n_tested, n_de, session_info (doi:10.1093/bib/bbz124)
report: reproducibility_record = session_info, seed, package_versions, collection_version, annotation_release (doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285)
steps.description: Final differential expression report with method, versions, design, thresholds, n_tested, n_de, and the sessionInfo reproducibility record.
acceptance_criteria: The report names the method, the version of each package, the design formula, the contrast, the thresholds, the number of genes tested, and the number of DE genes.
sessionInfo is attached and stored together with the results.
The TPM-only limitation (count models excluded, limma-trend route) is stated explicitly so a reader knows why a count model was not used.

plan.title: Psoriasis lesional vs control DE (limma on log2 TPM)
plan.analytical_narrative: The delivered data are a gene-level salmon TPM table (12000 genes x 12 samples: 6 psoriasis lesional vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch) with no raw counts and no quantification directories, so count models (DESeq2, edgeR, voom) are excluded by rule R-0004 and the sanctioned route is a limma linear model on log-scale values. Step 1 does sample-structure QC on log2(TPM+1) (MDS/PCA, sample distances, detected genes per R-0071) to confirm the 6 vs 6 condition split and surface any misclustered sample before any inference. Step 2 applies the TPM-specific procedure in order: a low-abundance floor (>=1 TPM in >=6 samples, the smallest group size, per R-0072 — limma has no independent filter, so filtering precedes the fit), no between-sample normalization because TPM already carries within-sample length/depth scaling (R-0073), an explicit control reference level with a named lesional/control contrast (R-0036), lmFit with eBayes(trend=TRUE, robust=TRUE) so hypervariable genes do not inflate the prior variance (R-0093), and selection by Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value < 0.05 (R-0043/R-0044); no LFC threshold was stated, so TREAT is not applied. Step 3 compiles the report with method, package versions, design, thresholds, n_tested, n_de, and the sessionInfo reproducibility record (R-0041/R-0086), and states the TPM-only limitation explicitly.
